thread:
sara: Quick intake here — new open-source conversational model candidate (fork-of-oxford-chat-2). Before we spin up evals/quant experiments, can legal/security confirm any license or usage restrictions? :eyes:

james (legal): Do we have a model_card or LICENSE file yet? Need to check whether the repo adds any non-commercial clauses or extra data-attribution requirements.

sara: Not attached yet. Repo link: https://git.internal/repos/forked-ox-chat-2 (internal mirror). I pasted the minimal model_card in #notes, will copy below.

raj: From infra/ops POV, we also need to know if we can run it in Dedicated/Private. If license forbids hosting on third-party infra we might need a private-only policy.

james (legal): Skimming the repo — there is an "additional_terms.md" referencing an NC (non-commercial) addendum for commercial productization. That blocks offering via Hosted API. Can still use in Private deployments for customers but must check distribution clause. I'll attach a short checklist: 1) Identify license SPDX; 2) Confirm clauses about commercial use; 3) Check model weights provenance (data source restrictions); 4) Any attribution requirement; 5) Derivative works language.

nisha (security): Also: does the model card mention sensitive data bleed (train sources)? If the training data has restricted datasets (medical/legal) there are compliance concerns for embeddings/PII leakage.

ben: For evals/quant we can run unit perf tests locally, but need to gate any public benchmarks we publish. If legal flags NC, we cannot publish benchmarks that look like product benchmarks without permission.

elaine: From product prioritization: this model has great latency/cost tradeoffs in initial tests. But if Hosted is off the table, revenue opportunity drops. We need a quick decision to prioritize other models for Hosted first.

license-bot: license-bot detected files: LICENSE (Apache-2.0), additional_terms.md (contains custom NC addendum). Action: manual review required.

james (legal): Confirmed — base is Apache-2.0 but the addendum purports to limit "commercial deployment as a SaaS product". That's a non-standard restriction layered on top of Apache. Need author contact or provenance docs.

sara: Proposed immediate actions (short checklist):
- sara: 1) Legal to confirm enforceability of addendum or request clarification from authors (assigned: james)
- sara: 2) Security to run data-provenance scan on weights repo and flag restricted datasets (assigned: nisha)
- sara: 3) ML to run internal evals/quant experiments in Private only env (assigned: raj + ben)
- sara: 4) Product to hold Hosted rollout until legal signoff (assigned: elaine)

raj: I'll spin up a Private-only eval rig and run fp16/4-bit quant sweep. Will post perf/quality delta summary. ETA: 48h. Using config: ```yaml
model: forked-ox-chat-2
precision: [fp16, int8_q4]
batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
metrics: [ppl, rouge, human-safety-checks]
```

ben: For quality regression tracking, I'll add a small eval set with known prompt failures and compare outputs side-by-side. Will include a toxicity check and hallucination probes.

nisha (security): Starting provenance scan now. If results show restricted dataset usage, we should mark the model as "compliance-blocked" for Hosted and Dedicated until resolved.

james (legal): I'll draft an email to the model authors requesting clarification and provenance docs. If they don't reply within 7 days we'll escalate to Product to deprioritize.

elaine: Thanks — product will freeze Hosted plans for this model. If legal clears with a permissive grant, we'll reprioritize.

sara: One more ask: can we add a short "onboarding license summary" to the model catalog meta if cleared? Something like: "Licensing notes: Apache-2.0 + author addendum restricting commercial SaaS; cleared for Private only until confirmed." That helps engineers avoid accidental Hosted deployments.

james (legal): Agreed. I'll prepare the summary text once I have author response.

license-bot: license-bot note: run `spdx-check --file model_card.json` and `provenance-scan --repo .` for a structured report.

sara: Perfect. I'll track tasks in the intake ticket and ping for updates. Thanks all :thumbsup:
